Re-measured at HEAD c981a3b1 (pushed; src/render, _harness/probe_crowd_accent.mjs and _harness/probe_body_lod.mjs clean in the working tree), on an idle machine (all 3 heavy slots free, load < 2). summary: Lane engine passes round 2: engine-lod is now done. The crowd's team-colour accents draw whole again, and I re-measured that three independent ways. (1) The code: crowd.ts bakeCrowd gives every part whose material is the accent a null LOD, so composeIndex keeps the accent's own triangles in the hull. In-page index counts show every accent part at full size: 708, 996, 750, 660, 714, 384, 294 and 144 indices, against 264 / 348 / 183 / 165 / 72 in round 1. Only the bodies (and the composed hulls) are LOD'd, e.g. 9249 -> 7053 and 7803 -> 4278 indices. (2) The engineers' probe_crowd_accent, re-run under my own tag, reproduces their numbers exactly. Shipped / full accent pixels are shieldwick 516 -> 522 (1.012), greatwick 1504 -> 1490 (0.991) and glimwick 782 -> 787 (1.006). The noise floor is 0 px, and the accent-LOD control (the regression) reads 0.205 / 0.686 / 0.784, so the probe does see the regression. (3) My own scratch A/B of round 1's frame (RIFT t 900 seed 7, the camera on the fight; it differs from round 1's full frame by only 127 px). The team-colour pixel count, measured with the same hue thresholds on round 1's shots, is blue 1251 full / 1253 shipped, where round 1 had 1063 for the regressed build. Orange is 3048 / 3056, where round 1 had 2845. Accent-mask pixels shipped / full are 1.000 (blue team) and 1.011 (orange team), and 1.012 at a closer zoom. At 2-3x the shieldwick stripes, greatwick hood bands and glimwick rings look identical to the full mesh, with no lock seams or holes. Cost and gates: perf_1080 --prod (my one sweep) GATE PASS. Match peak is 483,341 tris at 1084.2 s, which is <= 500k with a margin of 16.7k (the engineers' run gave 477,953). There are 40 programs (at the cap, as in round 1) and 273 draws; overBudget is empty and lateProgramsAfter60s is []. High reaches 60.1 fps with 0 dropped frames, cpu 2.34 ms and 257k tris; Low is 183k. dynres PASS, memory +2.0 % PASS (gate 3 %). probe_lod PASS (mean 0.096, over24 0.063 %, shadow share 0.272, console clean). probe_body_lod now passes --picks through to the bench, and it fails on an actor that is not drawn. With --no-reveal it exits 1 on exactly kemdo and tunlan (root/body visible false), the two empty crops from round 1. The default run and the --picks run both PASS with all 10 drawn each; together they cover all 16 fighters. Bodies go 197,279 -> 109,200 and 190,532 -> 105,542, and the menu draws 0 LOD1 bodies. typecheck: 0 errors. No regressions: only the crowd's body LOD changed (a vertex lock near the accents), fighters are unchanged, and the Wicks stay faceless.

items.evidence:
CODE (HEAD c981a3b1). src/render/crowd.ts bakeCrowd: `lods = meshes.map((m,i) => material.name === accentName ? null : lodIndex(m.geometry,'crowd',LOD.minTrisCrowd,units[i], accentLock(m, accents, LOD.crowdAccentLockM)))`, and `hull: composeIndex(..., (i) => lods[i]?.array ?? null)` keeps the accents' own triangles. accentLock reads world positions at rest, valid because actors.ts hullPlan calls scene.updateMatrixWorld(true) before bakeCrowd. src/render/lod.ts: LOD.crowdAccentLockM 0.035. lodIndex takes an optional `lock` and calls MeshoptSimplifier.simplifyWithAttributes(src, positions, 3, Float32Array(0), 0, [], lock, target, err, []), which meshoptimizer 1.3.0's asserts accept (vertex_lock Uint8Array of vertex count, empty attributes). Without a lock it is the unchanged plain simplify.

IN-PAGE INDEX COUNTS (scratch v2_crowd_accent_frame.mjs, log _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_frame.log). Every crowd_part_accent draws its full index, with no fullIndex swap: crowd_7 996, crowd_8 708, crowd_4 750, crowd_6 660, crowd_5 714, and the 384 / 294 / 144 parts. In round 1 these were 348 / 264 / 183 / 165 / 258 / 72. Only bodies are LOD'd (crowd_8 9249 -> 7053, crowd_7 7560 -> 5391, crowd_4 7803 -> 4278, crowd_6 7770 -> 5583) and the composed hulls (e.g. 9957 -> 7761).

ACCENT A/B, ENGINEERS' PROBE RE-RUN. `node _harness/probe_crowd_accent.mjs --tag integ2_engine_v2` PASS (_harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_crowd_accent.{json,log}; sheets _harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v2_accent_<def>_<team>.png). Body parts 13,403 -> 8,822 tris (0.658); 16 accent parts, 2,134 tris, all whole. Shipped / full: shieldwick 516 -> 522 (1.012), greatwick 1504 -> 1490 (0.991), glimwick 782 -> 787 (1.006). Per crop the range is 0.989-1.015, the floor 0 px everywhere. The control with the accents through LOD.crowd reads 0.205 / 0.686 / 0.784 (a shieldwick team-1 crop drops to 0.039), so the gate is sensitive. I read the probe: the accent px are the pixels that change by more than 24 levels when only the accent meshes are hidden, so they measure the stripe as drawn after the body's occlusion. That is what a sinking or bulging body LOD would change.

INDEPENDENT A/B, ROUND 1'S FRAME. Scratch v2_crowd_accent_frame.mjs + v2_accent_count.py → _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_frame_accent_count.json. Shots _harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v2_{frame,close}_{full,shipped}_{acc,noacc}.png. The frame is the same as round 1's (127 px > 24 vs integ2_engine_v1_accent_full.png). The team-colour pixel counts use round 1's hue thresholds; for comparison round 1 counted full / regressed / accents whole without the lock. Blue team region: v2 full 1251 / v2 shipped 1253 (r1: 1251 / 1063 / 1289). Orange team region: 3048 / 3056 (r1: 3049 / 2845 / 3093). The lock removes the +3 % over-show that accents-whole-alone had. Accent-mask px shipped / full: blue 1155 / 1155 (1.000), orange 1718 / 1737 (1.011). Closer zoom: 3987 / 4033 (1.012); colour-filtered 1.006 / 1.005. Visual at 2-3x (_harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v2_close_ab_{blue,orange}.png, full above, shipped below): the shieldwick stripes and hood dots, the greatwick hood bands and the glimwick lantern rings match the full mesh, with no dashes, gaps, lock seams or holes. Fighter pixels are identical across the probe's states (Ervet torso mean 152.6/147.2/139.0 in all four).

PERF, my one sweep. `node _harness/perf_1080.mjs --prod --out _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_perf_1080.json` (.log; prod bench rebuilt from HEAD) GATE PASS. Match peak is 483,341 tris at 1084.2 s, <= 500k with 16.7k of margin. The engineers' run gave 477,953 and round 1 gave 451,815; the +31.5k is the accents and locked rims drawn whole. Peak frame: actors 324k/158. Draws 273 at 1088.2 s; programs 40 at 15.2 s (<= 40, unchanged from round 1). overBudget tris / draws / programs are all [] and lateProgramsAfter60s is []. High: 60.1 fps, 0 dropped, p95 16.8 ms, cpu 2.34 ms, 174 draws, 37 programs, 257k tris; timing measured (load 0.88 -> 1.54). Low: 60.1 fps, 183k tris. dynres PASS (scale 1). memory +2.0 % PASS (<= 3 %).

probe_lod: `node _harness/probe_lod.mjs --no-build --out _harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_lod.json` PASS. meanAbsDiff 0.096, over24 0.063 %, shadow share 0.272, frame 310,901 -> 233,028, console clean.

PROBE_BODY_LOD. (a) The guard: `--no-reveal --tag integ2_engine_v2_noreveal` exits 1 with 'kemdo (A/B/A2): not drawn (root/body visible false...)' and 'tunlan (A/B/A2): not drawn (... fighters main 0 tris)' (_harness/_reports/integ2_engine_v2_noreveal_body_lod.log). Those are exactly round 1's two empty crops, so an invisible actor now FAILS. (b) Default `--tag integ2_engine_v2_p1` PASS: all 10 drawn (ervet, odrum, burdam, marund, vashil, kemdo, tunlan, hesmi, rishal, dunsom); bodies 197,279 -> 109,200 (0.554). Tunlan 20,926 -> 8,405 and Kemdo 18,089 -> 11,736 are now real crops (_harness/_shots/integ2_engine_v2_p1_bodylod_{tunlan,kemdo}.png: the character is drawn, the faces / hat are identical A|B). (c) `--picks ardit,ilsheta,lisvel,nurrow,sukri,ulkro,kemdo,tunlan,ervet,odrum --tag integ2_engine_v2_p2` PASS, the bench honouring picks (seat 0 ardit). Bodies 190,532 -> 105,542; Ilsheta 17,004 -> 7,736. The two runs cover all 16 fighters. Menu: 0 LOD1 bodies in both. typecheck: `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

minors: perf_1080 --prod: programs sit exactly at the <= 40 cap (40 at 15.2 s), as in round 1, and the match peak margin narrowed from 48k to 16.7k triangles (483,341 / 500k) now that the crowd accents draw whole. The gate passes; the next renderer feature that adds a program or ~17k peak triangles will fail it.
